amendments.reason: Added anchor_change.enforced_by, a self-describing field naming the refusal that makes decided_before_any_stage2_adapter true (main() evaluates adapters_exist() first, before any flag including --refreeze), and made that field the constant True rather than a re-evaluated call so --check-only cannot mismatch after the control trains. No criterion, anchor value, epsilon, tie-break, grid row or mechanism changed; this edit predates every Stage-2 adapter.

Corrected the cache-cost paragraph in preservation_anchor.py's docstring. It carried pre-build estimates (1,434 rows of 248,077 log-probabilities, 1.42 GB, ~7.8 positions per example) that the built cache contradicts on every figure: the committed sidecar records 1,489 positions, vocab 248,320, 1.479 GB, 8.14 per example. Comment-only; no code, criterion, anchor value, epsilon, tie-break, grid row or mechanism changed, and no Stage-2 adapter exists yet. tests/unit/test_iteration12_stage2.py now reads those four figures back from the sidecar so they cannot drift again.

Replaced the faithfulness control's comparison basis after it ran and refused, and disclosed why. THE CONTROL AS FIRST FROZEN gated on reproducing the adapter Stage 1 FILED, byte for byte, by sha256 over the directory. It ran for 1187.8 s over 230 optimizer steps and refused: digest d6b968164c0222dd against filed 846f585a8e909d0b, with an identical recipe in all fifteen fields, an identical init adapter, and epoch means differing from epoch 1 at about 1e-3. Per-file comparison narrowed it to adapter_config.json differing ONLY in the ORDER of the same seven target modules. THAT ORDER IS NOT REPRODUCIBLE: PeftConfig.target_modules is a Python set, and Python randomises the string hash seed per process unless PYTHONHASHSEED is exported, so the order PEFT serialises it in -- and the LoRA injection order behind it, which decides which module draws which dropout mask -- varies run to run. Four seeds were measured to give four different orders over the same seven modules, a pinned seed gives one order every time, and the filed order matched none of the seven seeds tried, so the process that wrote it is not recoverable. TO ESTABLISH THAT THIS INDICTS THE CRITERION AND NOT THE NEW LOOP, unlearning_trainer.train_unlearning -- hash-bound, unedited -- was re-run on the same spec from the same init adapter. It did not reproduce the filed adapter either, and landed the same distance from it: max per-tensor weight gap 1.726e-03 for the frozen re-run against filed, 1.812e-03 for the new loop against filed, 1.800e-03 between the two re-runs, over 256 tensors. Three gaps of one order, so the new loop is no further from the filed adapter than the frozen loop is from a file the frozen loop itself wrote. The three adapters hold the same seven target modules in three different orders. WHAT REPLACES IT: --control now trains the incumbent objective three times in ONE process under ONE pinned PYTHONHASHSEED -- A through the frozen loop, A2 through the frozen loop again to MEASURE the noise floor rather than assume it, B through train_with_preservation with every group plain sft/gd and neither cap nor anchor. The gate is that gap(A, B) does not exceed gap(A, A2), with bitwise equality demanded outright when the floor is exactly zero, compared per tensor rather than by digest because a digest says "different" and cannot distinguish float noise from a different objective. The filed adapter is still loaded, compared and REPORTED beside the gate; it is simply not what the gate reads. scripts/lanes/iter12_stage2.sh exports PYTHONHASHSEED and train_iter12_stage2.py refuses to run the control without it. WHY THIS IS NOT A RULE MOVED TO FIT A RESULT: the retired criterion was unsatisfiable by construction, so it tested the interpreter's hash seed rather than the two loops, and a gate that cannot pass says nothing when it fails. The control produced no candidate, no prediction, no retention number and no score, so there was no result for the anchor, its values, the eight numbers, the epsilon, the tie-break, the grid or the mechanisms to have been fitted to -- and this amendment touches none of them, only faithfulness_control.* and the three protocol hashes. The failed control and the frozen-loop re-run were MOVED to outputs/superseded/iter12_stage2_control_v1/ rather than deleted, with a README recording the digests, the three gaps and the three target_modules orders, and the small files committed so the disclosure is inspectable from a clone rather than asserted. Seven tests now pin the amended control STRUCTURALLY by parsing scripts/train_iter12_stage2.py, because widening what an amendment may touch needs something holding the other side: the hash seed is checked before anything trains, three runs happen with the frozen loop twice, the gate has exactly three branches and never assigns passed a bare True, the filed adapter never reaches passed, and main refuses to train when the gate did not pass.

Added faithfulness_control.what_pins_this_in_the_suite and why_those_tests_are_listed_here, and CORRECTED A COUNT THE PREVIOUS AMENDMENT'S REASON GOT WRONG. That reason said "Seven tests now pin the amended control STRUCTURALLY". There are eight: test_the_gate_compares_the_right_pair_of_runs_on_each_side was written after the reason was drafted, to close a hole the other seven left -- the gate could be fed the wrong PAIR of runs through the across/floor bindings and still branch three ways, still never assign passed a bare True, and still never read the filed adapter by name, so nothing else would have caught a control whose noise floor was measured as A against B and whose across-gap was measured as A against A2, i.e. one that compares each quantity with itself and passes always. WHY THE LIST IS IN THE FREEZE: replacing this control's criterion widened what a later amendment may touch to include faithfulness_control.*, so the seal needs something holding the other side. Naming the eight tests that hold it, in the frozen document rather than in prose, makes the disclosure checkable from a clone -- a test reads the list back against tests/unit/test_iteration12_stage2.py and fails if the two differ, and fails if the list names a test that does not exist -- and makes a later amendment that quietly drops one visible as a change to this field rather than as a silence. WHY THE CORRECTION IS HERE AND NOT IN THE PREVIOUS ENTRY: that entry is a historical record of why the third amendment was made, and rewriting it to say eight would make the record agree with the code at the cost of no longer being a record. Correcting forward leaves both facts visible. NO CRITERION MOVED: this amendment touches only faithfulness_control.* and the hash of scripts/freeze_iter12_stage2.py; the anchor, its values, the eight numbers, the epsilon, the tie-break, the grid, the mechanisms and the inherited generation contract are all unchanged.

gpu_hours_estimated: about 10: seven trainings at 24-40 minutes each plus seven generations at a 40.2-minute median, on a box where only one GPU currently has the ~26 GiB the recipe needs

what_is_frozen.primary_rule: candidate >= MG - epsilon on all eight numbers; a number missing on either side disqualifies
what_is_frozen.computed_by: route_stratified_retention.floor_check_stratified -- the same frozen function Stage 1c used, with MG's vector passed as the baseline. That function is generic in its baseline, so no new metric code was written and none was edited.
what_is_frozen.among_eligible: minimise D_G with the frozen tie-break, exactly as Stage 1 did. The floor decides eligibility; D_G only orders the eligible.

anchor_change.enforced_by: main() evaluates adapters_exist() first and unconditionally, before any flag including --refreeze
anchor_change.pre_registered_by: README.md, which states that Stage 2 faces the same anchor and will return the no-op again unless the anchor itself is reconsidered, and that this is a design decision to make before Stage 2 is frozen, not after it is scored.

matched_comparison.what_this_isolates: MG and MF are trained by one recipe on datasets whose 387 retained completions are identical and whose 90 target completions all differ, and both cover the probe half. Their retention difference is therefore the cost of the granularity transformation itself, with recipe, retained knowledge and information held equal -- not a cost of unlearning from MF.

the_oracle_fails_the_frozen_floor.why_this_decides_it: D_G, the selection criterion this project has used since Iteration 9, measures distance TO MG. A floor whose reference point MG itself fails disqualifies the state the criterion is aiming at, so it can only rank candidates by how little they did.

re_anchoring_changes_no_filed_verdict.why_this_matters: A rule change that turned filed failures into passes would be a goalpost move. This one turns none: Stage 1 is 0 of 8 eligible under either anchor.

the_new_floor_does_not_licence_inaction.why_this_matters: Under the MG anchor the no-op is not eligible either, so the rule cannot be satisfied by declining to unlearn -- the failure mode the B0 anchor had.

anchor_change.the_frozen_stage1c_floor_is_untouched: route_stratified_retention.py and analyze_iter12_route_stratified.py are hash-bound by the Stage-1c freeze and are not edited. The filed Stage-1, Stage-1b and Stage-1c reports are byte-identical, and their B0-anchored verdicts stand as filed.
anchor_change.a_defect_left_in_place: route_stratified_retention.floor_check_stratified labels its baseline field 'b0' and its comparison string 'candidate >= b0 - eps' regardless of which baseline is passed. That module is hash-bound by the Stage-1c freeze, so the names cannot be corrected; under Stage 2's primary gate the field named 'b0' holds MG's values, and the Stage-2 report says so explicitly.

mechanisms.preregistered_by: scripts/freeze_iter12_selection_protocol.py, whose stage_2 block names the mechanism and whose stage2_gate reports stage2_opens true; retention_selection.stage2_gate's own docstring asks 'Does the MF-preservation regularizer stage open?'

trained.B5_bounded_ascent: the incumbent recipe with -lambda * NLL(fine_target) replaced by -lambda * min(NLL(fine_target), cap), whose gradient is exactly zero above the cap. Targets the coordinate the measurement says governs, and decouples how far to suppress from how long to train, which Stage 1 coupled through the epoch count.
trained.B6_mf_preservation_anchor: the preregistered regularizer: KL(p_MF || p_theta) over the supervised positions of the fit-half retain group, at the beta the calibration derived. Trained because an observational argument over eight points is not an experiment, and a mechanism this study was preregistered with deserves to be run rather than argued away.
trained.B6R_hybrid: replay and the anchor on the same forward pass, through anchor_weight rather than a second group entry, so the epoch keeps its 363 micro-batches and the schedule under test does not move.

mechanisms.capped_term: -lambda * min(NLL(fine_target), cap), whose gradient is exactly zero above the cap; verified on a stub model before this freeze was written
mechanisms.anchor_term: beta * KL(p_MF || p_theta) over supervised positions
mechanisms.anchor_direction: KL(p_MF || p_theta), exact over the full vocabulary

beta_star_derivation.beta_star_is: the strength at which beta * KL(p_MF || p_candidate) equals lambda * avg_loss_fine_target at the END of the incumbent reference row's training, i.e. the anchor term is exactly as large as the term it is meant to bound
beta_star_derivation.why_these_multipliers: 1.5 orders of magnitude centred on the incumbent's operating point. A sweep narrower than that could sit entirely on one side of the transition between 'the anchor does nothing' and 'the anchor prevents the transformation', and neither end would be measured.
beta_star_derivation.derived_from: committed training summaries and measured KL only; no retention number, prediction parquet or evaluation query

mechanisms.why_the_anchor_is_trained_anyway: The calibration argues it cannot work: its optimum is MF, which is no unlearning, and states at equal drift from MF differ in retention by far more than the floor resolves. That is an observational argument over eight points. A mechanism this study was preregistered with gets run rather than argued away, and if the argument is wrong the run is what finds out.

grid.cap_units: nats of per-token NLL on the fine completion

the_frozen_validator_was_run.filtered_because: candidate_grid.py is hash-bound, so its METHODS tuple and its mode vocabulary were frozen before Stage 2 existed and cannot be extended. Only 'unknown method' and 'bad mode' are filtered, by exact substring, and the residual must be empty -- so every other structural check the frozen validator makes still applies to this grid.

faithfulness_control.what_it_is: train_with_preservation is a second copy of a training loop, because unlearning_trainer.train_unlearning is hash-bound and cannot grow a mode. --control trains the incumbent Stage-1 objective THREE times in ONE process under ONE pinned PYTHONHASHSEED: A through the frozen loop, A2 through the frozen loop again, B through the new loop with every group in a plain sft/gd mode and neither a cap nor an anchor.
faithfulness_control.spec_read_from: the frozen Stage-1 grid, not retyped
faithfulness_control.the_gate: A2 exists to MEASURE the noise floor rather than assume it: gap(A, A2) is how far two runs of the same code land apart on this stack. The gate is that gap(A, B) does not exceed it -- and bitwise equality is demanded outright when the floor is exactly zero, which is what one process and a pinned seed are supposed to buy. A sha256 alone cannot express this: it says 'different' and stops, so it cannot distinguish float noise from a different objective, which is the whole question. The control therefore compares per-tensor gaps and reports the worst tensor.
faithfulness_control.it_is_a_gate_not_a_report: scripts/train_iter12_stage2.py refuses to train a single candidate unless the control passed, so a drift between the two loops stops the study instead of being interpreted as a difference between mechanisms.
faithfulness_control.cpu_half_already_verified: tests/unit/test_iteration12_stage2.py drives both loops against one stub model and asserts bit-identical parameters, forward-call counts, optimizer steps and epoch summaries, so a divergence is caught without a GPU as well.
faithfulness_control.control_dir_is_inside_the_refusal: The control's adapters live under the Stage-2 checkpoint root, so running it locks this freeze against amendment. That is deliberate: a control run under an unfrozen loop proves nothing about the frozen one.
faithfulness_control.a_criterion_this_replaced: The control as first frozen compared ONE run of the new loop against the adapter Stage 1 FILED, by sha256 over the whole directory. It ran, and refused: identical recipe in all fifteen fields, identical init adapter, identical 230 optimizer steps, and adapter_config.json differing only in the ORDER of the same seven target modules. That order is not reproducible. PeftConfig.target_modules is a Python set, and Python randomises the string hash seed per process unless PYTHONHASHSEED is exported, so the serialised order -- and the LoRA injection order behind it, which decides which module draws which dropout mask -- varies run to run. Four seeds were measured to give four different orders, a pinned seed gives one order every time, and the filed order matched none of the seven seeds tried, so the process that wrote it is not recoverable.
faithfulness_control.the_evidence_that_it_was_the_stack_not_t: The FROZEN loop, unedited and hash-bound, was re-run on the same spec from the same init adapter. It did not reproduce the filed adapter either, and landed the same distance from it: max per-tensor weight gap 1.726e-03 for the frozen re-run against filed, 1.812e-03 for the new loop against filed, 1.800e-03 between the two re-runs -- three gaps of one order, so the new loop is no further from the filed adapter than the frozen loop is from itself. All three adapters hold the same seven target modules in three different orders. Both runs are kept under outputs/superseded/iter12_stage2_control_v1/, whose README.md records the orders and the gaps.
faithfulness_control.why_replacing_it_is_not_moving_the_goalp: The retired criterion was unsatisfiable by construction, so it tested the interpreter's hash seed rather than the two loops, and a gate that cannot pass says nothing when it fails. The replacement asks the question the original was written to ask -- do the two copies compute the same function? -- and asks it in the only way that has an answer, with the environment held still and the noise floor measured instead of assumed. The filed adapter is still loaded, compared and REPORTED beside the gate, so its gap stays visible; it is simply not what the gate reads. Nothing about the anchor, the eight numbers, the epsilon, the tie-break, the grid or the mechanisms moved: the control produced no candidate, no prediction, no retention number and no score, so there was no result for any of them to be fitted to. What changed is a fact about the apparatus. The failed control's directory was MOVED to outputs/superseded rather than deleted, so the adapter that demonstrated the defect is still on disk and inspectable.
faithfulness_control.the_hash_seed_is_pinned_by_the_lane_scri: scripts/lanes/iter12_stage2.sh exports PYTHONHASHSEED, and train_iter12_stage2.py refuses to run the control at all without it, because a control under a randomised seed measures the seed.
faithfulness_control.why_those_tests_are_listed_here: Replacing this control's criterion widened what a later amendment may touch to include faithfulness_control.*, so the seal needs something holding the other side. These eight tests are that. They are STRUCTURAL rather than behavioural because the script imports the trainers at module level and CI installs a closure without torch: each parses scripts/train_iter12_stage2.py and asserts which branch does what -- that the hash seed is checked first, that three runs happen with the frozen loop twice, that each side of the gate is built from the right pair of them, that the gate has exactly three branches and never assigns a bare True, that the filed adapter never reaches it, and that main refuses to train both when the gate failed and when the control was never run. Naming them here rather than describing them in prose makes the list checkable against the test file, and makes a later amendment that quietly drops one visible as a change to this field. One of them is not purely structural: test_an_unpinned_hash_seed_refuses_rather_than_measuring_the_interpreter lifts that single function out by ast.get_source_segment and EXECUTES it, because 'there is a raise statement somewhere in here' passes just as happily for 'if False: raise'.

evidence_base.never_read_enforced_by: scripts/train_iter12_stage2.py and scripts/select_iter12_stage2.py refuse any argument that resolves inside those paths, on RESOLVED paths rather than on strings, and write only under the Stage-2 checkpoint and predictions directories.
evidence_base.probe_half_never_rehearsed: The preserve group covers 0 of the 204 probe-half associations, recorded in the basis and re-checked by the matched comparison. An anchor fitted on probe-half prompts would rehearse the quantity the floor measures.

calibration_controls.why_these_matter: Both are exactly zero, so the extraction, the position shift and the KL are measuring what they claim before any difference between adapters is read as one.

what_the_ceiling_means.why: retain_other reaches only 23 probe donor entities, so its largest possible denominator in this dataset is 228 queries and its best possible row-micro resolution is 0.0043859649. The pool is exhausted: 90 target plus 387 retained associations account for all 477, so there is no reserve to draw a larger probe from.
what_the_ceiling_means.consequence: Stage 1c roughly doubles the frozen basis and makes both parents' shortfalls exceed their between-seed spread, but it does not make retain-other well powered. A mechanism whose retention effect is smaller than about 0.0043859649 cannot be resolved on this dataset at all, at any number of seeds.

measurement_limits.retain_other_stays_weakly_powered: 23 probe donors and 38 queries per split, 228 at the absolute ceiling, so one flipped outcome is 0.0132 and no number of seeds changes that.
measurement_limits.the_ceiling_is_the_dataset: The association pool is exhausted -- 90 target plus 387 retained is all 477 -- and query_generation.py is one of the eighteen paths the confirmation freeze sealed.
measurement_limits.one_seed_is_not_enough: Stage 1b measured a between-seed sd of 0.0120 to 0.0515 on these numbers, which exceeds the retain-other resolution. Stage 2 trains one seed per row, so a row that clears the primary gate by less than that spread is a candidate for replication rather than a result, and the report must say so instead of ranking on it.

extends.note: Stage 2 extends the Stage-1c floor to a different anchor and reuses two of the parquets that freeze bound. It re-decides nothing that was filed: the B0-anchored verdicts stand, and they are recomputed and reported beside the new ones.

reused_predictions_bound.why_reused: All three parquets are bound by sha256 in the Stage-1c freeze under the single verified contract. Regenerating them would spend about two GPU-hours producing a second draw from identical adapter bytes, and would put fresh files where hashed evidence already sits. The selector re-derives each state's eight numbers from the reused bytes and refuses to write unless all of them equal the values Stage 1c filed, so reuse is checked rather than trusted.
reused_predictions_bound.note: Gitignored and therefore absent from a clone. Verified apart from the rest of the freeze, reporting match, mismatch or absent per path.

sidecar.kl_direction: KL(p_MF || p_theta), exact over the full vocabulary

reference_cache_bound.why_bound: The anchor rows train against these bytes. A cache rebuilt from a different MF adapter, or at a different truncation length, would preserve a different function, and the resulting adapter would look perfectly ordinary.
reference_cache_bound.note: Gitignored: 1.48 GB of fp32 log-probabilities. Verified apart from the rest of the freeze, reporting match, mismatch or absent per path.

contract.why_not_the_pilot_predictions_dir: Both grids contain a candidate called B0. In one directory the two studies would share the filename predictions_tv_B0.parquet, and a differing experiment_id would make the sidecar refuse reuse and REGENERATE over committed pilot-100 evidence. A separate directory makes that impossible rather than unlikely.

generation_contract_inherited.why_it_is_load_bearing: Stage 2 generates predictions for its own candidates and reads two of Stage 1's. The image route is the one whose correctness flips when batch composition changes -- 15 flips out of 4,518 between two B0 parquets from identical adapter bytes, all of them image-route -- so a contract difference between the reused and the generated parquets would put the anchor and the candidates on two instruments. The selector refuses a run whose contract differs.

disclosure.why_that_is_not_a_goalpost_move: Three properties, all computed in the basis rather than asserted: the new anchor is justified by a comparison that needs no prediction at all (MG and MF have byte-identical retained training data); it changes no filed verdict, because Stage 1 is 0 of 8 eligible under either anchor; and it does not licence inaction, because B0 itself fails it on 2 of 8.
disclosure.cap_range_disclosure: The caps bracket the oracle's measured level from both sides and reach into the range the Stage-1 candidates actually occupied. The range was chosen AFTER measuring MG's level, which is disclosed here rather than left implicit; what is not true is that any oracle value enters the training procedure, because the cap is a swept constant and MG's 1.3643 appears in no candidate's spec. The sweep's uncapped end is the incumbent Stage-1 row, which already exists with predictions on disk and costs nothing.
disclosure.direction_is_against_interest: The new anchor is HARDER on the rows that matter: the candidates that came closest under B0 are not the ones that come closest under MG, and the cap sweep's own uncapped point is an existing Stage-1 row that fails.
disclosure.what_this_legitimately_preregisters: Stage 3: the next mechanism is judged on all eight numbers against the anchor frozen here, and its protocol is frozen before it is trained.
